plan.nickname: Soledad "Kindly" Mwangi, a ring name she chose herself and puts on everything; Ines fights as "The Valet" after her old job parking cars at the casino
plan.detail: Ines took her daughter Pia out of Soledad's Tuesday 4:15 kids' class without a word; Pia's gi stayed on peg nine

opener.text: Ref, first of all, thank you. You got there. Eventually.
Thank you, sir, for coming over. Both of those last two, you were on your way. I saw you. On your way.
And thank you to her corner for the towel. Beautiful towel. Never left his shoulder.
Thank you, Ines, for keeping your hands that low. Honestly. It made my night so easy.

personal.text: You took Pia out of my four-fifteen without a word, Ines. So thank you for teaching me how it's done. Tonight I didn't say a word either. Twice.
She knelt first. Pia used to do that every Tuesday, bow at the door. Then one Tuesday no bow, no text, just peg nine with a gi on it. Thank you for the bow, Ines. Took you a year.
Hands up, eyes front, flat on her back with a perfect guard. I taught that to Pia at four-fifteen on Tuesdays. Nice to see somebody in the family kept it.
For the record, Pia's gi is still on peg nine. Nobody told me she wasn't coming back. Ref, you were late too, but at least you showed up.

closer.text: That's everything. Thank you for everything, Ines. Truly. Peg nine's still open on Tuesdays.
Report ends. Fighter thanked. Kids' class resumes Tuesday at four-fifteen. She knows where the door is.
Tell Pia her spot's still hers. Free for any kid whose mom just learned to stay down.
Dario says thanks, by the way. He taught you to wait on the towel. He watched this one from my corner.
